( Reaffirmed 2001 ) 
Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
PLIERS, PLATE, DENTAL 

( First Revision ) 



1- Scope — Specifies material, dimensions and other requirements of plate pliers used in dentistry. 

2. Material — Stainless steel of designation 30Cr13 conforming to IS: 6603-1972 'Specification for 
stainless steel bars and flats'. 

3. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1 to 3. 

3.1 Tolerances on linear dimensions shall be permitted as follows: 

a) ;fc 01 mm on dimensions up to 20 mm; 

b) ± 02 mm on dimensions above 2*0 mm and up to 5*0 mm; 

c) ± 05 mm on dimensions above 50 mm and up to 20*0 mm; 

d) ± 10 mm on dimensions above 200 mm and up to 50 mm; 

e) ± 2'0 mm on dimensions above 50*0 mm and up to 1000 mm; and 

f) ± 2 5 mm on dimensions above 100*0 mm. 

3.2 Tolerances on angular dimensions shall be ± 1°. 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The two halves of the pliers shall move fully and freely at the joint without any play. The jaws 
shall register accurately on closing the pliers. 

4.2 The joint shall be flat box type joint shown in Fig. 1. The pin shall be rivetted and finished flush 
with the surface. 

4.3 The pliers shall be free from sharp edges, pits, burrs, cracks and other surface defects. All the edges 
except the working end shall be rounded. 

4.4 The surface of the pliers shall be finished smooth. 

4.5 The pliers shall be polished bright and passivated except the outside surface of the handle which 
may have a matt finish, by treating them in 10 percent (viv) nitric acid solution for not less 
than 30 min at a temperature of not less then 10°C and not exceeding 60°C. The pliers shall then 
be rinsed in water, dried in hot air and the joint lightly lubricated with a non-toxic and non-corrosive 
substance. 

5. Heat Treatment — The pliers shall be uniformly hardened and tempered to a hardness 
of 400 to 480 HV, when tested in accordance with IS : 1501 1968 Method for Vickers hardness test for 
steel ( first revision )'. 

6. Tests 

6.1 Practical Test — The pliers shall be used to band and shape a wire 1 mm in diameter and made of 
stainless steel of designation 04Cr18Ni10 or 07Cr18Ni9 of IS : 6528-1972 'Specification for stainless 
steel wire'. This shall be done six times. The pliers shall show no sign of damage after the test. 

6.2 Elasticity Test — The pliers shall be made to grip a piece of 1 mm thick hardened steel bit having a 
minimum hardness of 250 HV. A compressive force of 200 N ( 20 kgf approx ) shall be applied to the 
pliers and allowed to act for 5 min in such a manner that the force acts on each arm of the handle 
[ a total of 400 N ( 40 kgf approx ) on the instrument ] at a distance of 40 mm from its free end. The 
pliers shall not show any sign of damage or acquire a permanent set after the test. 



Adopted 28 February 1985

IS : 4313 - 1985 

6.3 Corrosion Resistance Test — The pliers shall be tested in accordance with IS : 7531-1975 'Method 
for boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of stainless steel surgical instruments'. It shall 
show no sign of corrosion after the test. 

7. Marking — Each plier shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's name, initials 
cr registered trade-mark; name of the plier and its number; the words 'Stainless Steel', and the country 
of manufacture. 

7.1 ISI Certification Mark — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — Each plier shall be wrapped either in a polyethylene bag or a wax paper. It shall then 
be packed in cartons in accordance with the current trade practice. The carton shall bear the name of 
the plier; manufacturer's name, initials or registered trade-mark; the words 'Stainless Steel' and the 
country of manufacture. 

8.1 Alternatively, it may be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 

9. Sampling 

9.1 Sampling procedure and acceptance criteria for the plier shall be as agreed to between the 
purchaser and the supplier. A recommended scheme for the same is given in Appendix A. 



APPENDIX A 

(Clause 9.1) 

SAMPLING SCHEME AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY, FOR 
PLIERS, PLATE, DENTAL 

A-1. Lot — In any consignment all the pliers produced from the same material under similar 
conditions shall constitute a lot. 

A-2. The number of pliers to be selected from each lot shall depend upon the size of the lot and shall 
be in accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 1. 

TABLE 1 SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 

Lot Size Sample Size 

(D (2) 

UP to 15 2 

16 „ 50 3 

51 „ 150 5 

151 and above 8 

A-2.1 These pliers shall be selected from the lot at random and in order to ensure the randomness 
of selection, procedures given in IS : 4905-1968 'Methods for random sampling' may be allowed. 

A-3. Number of Tests and Criteria for Conformity — All the piiers selected at random in accordance 
with col 1 and 2 of Table 1 shall be tested for shape and dimensions, workmanship and finish, heat 
treatment, practical test, elasticity test, and corrosion resistance test. The lot shall be considered as 
conforming to these requirements if none of the pliers in the sample is found to be defective in any of 
these tests. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was first published in 1967. The present revision has been undertaken to bring 
it in line with the current trade practices prevalent in the dental instruments industry. 

In this revision, tolerances on linear and angular dimensions, proper references to raw materials 
and sampling plan have been specified. 



Printed at Arcee Press, New Delhi, India
